subject: Exec approval requested: Skyline Health - pricing & terms deviations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Exec approval requested: Skyline Health - pricing & terms deviations

Team,

Quick summary: Skyline Health wants to finalize a two-year committed deployment (production staging + 10 dedicated GPUs) and has pushed back hard on our standard liability cap and indemnity language. They are also asking for a one-time 35% first-year discount to accelerate their purchase order (PO expected by 5/22).

What they want (high level):
- Liability cap: remove cap for IP claims and increase general cap to unlimited for breach of contract language (they redlined our SOW)
- Indemnity: broader third-party IP indemnity, carve-outs for subsidiary claims
- Warranty: limit our warranty remedies to refund only (they want to remove SLA credits)
- Commercial: 35% off list price year 1, then 10% year 2 with annual renewal at list

Attachments: Skyline_SOW_redline_v3.pdf (redlines), pricing_summary_SKY-2028-043.xlsx (price / margin impact), impact_model_Q1-Q2.csv (financials)

Why I’m escalating: legal flags the indemnity and IP carveouts as high risk; commercial operations flagged margin erosion > 40% in year 1 with the 35% discount and dedicated capacity commitments. They are timing-sensitive — procurement indicated the PO will land if we accept their redlines this week.

Ask:
- Legal (Jonas): recommend an executive position we can take (specific cap values / indemnity carve-outs acceptable to us)
- Aditya/Laura: signoff or veto on the 35% one-time discount and whether we tie it to a firm 24-month revenue commitment + non-cancellable clause

I’ve attached the redlines and the pricing impact model. If we can get a yes/no by EOD Tuesday (5/16 PST) I’ll route to procurement and counter with a tracked DocuSign packet.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-15T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Exec approval requested: Skyline Health - pricing & terms deviations

Marissa —

Thanks for the background and the redline. Quick legal read (high level):

1) Liability cap: their redline removes the cap for IP and puts an unlimited exposure on certain breach scenarios. We cannot accept uncapped exposure. Reasonable path: a single aggregate cap tied to fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim or a fixed cap (I recommend $2,000,000 given the size of the deal).

2) IP indemnity: Their language attempts to extend indemnity to downstream affiliates and to any claim arising from combined use with third-party systems. We can narrow to (a) claims alleging our breach of the license grant or infringement by our delivered model and (b) exclude claims arising from customer modifications or third-party integrations.

3) Warranty: the removal of SLA remedies is acceptable only if we preserve our SLA credit structure and limit credits to a percentage of monthly fees (cap at one month’s payment). We should refuse a refund-only remedy.

4) Broad definitions: several catch-all terms expand scope ("affiliates", "derivative products"). We should tighten definitions and add a mutual indemnity clause for customer IP claims tied to customer-provided data.

My recommendation for exec signoff items:
- Authorize cap at $2,000,000 aggregate (all claims except gross negligence/IP may be separate negotiated carve-outs)
- Accept narrowed IP indemnity language (we propose redline attached)
- Keep SLA credits as sole commercial remedy limited to 1x monthly fees

If the execs want a lower cap we need to quantify residual risk; ops should provide margin/expected loss at $1M vs $2M to guide.

I’ve tracked proposed redlines in Skyline_SOW_redline_v3.pdf and flagged the clauses that require commercial approval.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

+1 on Jonas’ legal framing. A couple commercial datapoints to help execs decide:

- Baseline ARR impact: Year 1 revenue with 35% discount = $680k (list would be ~$1.05M). Year 2 at 10% = $945k. Two-year committed revenue ~ $1.625M.
- OpEx note: dedicated GPUs and priority routing add fixed monthly costs that make a deep first-year discount painful without a firm non-cancelable commitment.

Compromise we can offer without additional risk:
- Approve 35% discount for year 1 only if: customer signs 24-month MSAs with non-cancellable minimums equal to 90% of committed spend for year 1, and they prepay at least 50% of year 1 fees at signing.
- Accept Jonas’ proposed $2M liability cap and narrowed IP indemnity (as redlined)
- Preserve SLA credits (cap at one month) and expressly exclude transformative third-party integrations from our indemnity scope

If execs want to reduce the cap to $1M, we should require a revenue-based escrow or insurance endorsement.

If we get a verbal OK I’ll prepare the DocuSign counter and attach the pricing table. Tom Ellis has indicated the PO will be submitted this week if we move quickly.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Exec approval requested: Skyline Health - pricing & terms deviations

Team —

Appreciate the quick analysis. I’m willing to authorize the following, conditionally, so we can keep the deal moving:

1) Liability cap: approve $2,000,000 aggregate cap. This will be the public-facing number in the counteroffer. Any request for an uncapped IP exposure is a hard no.

2) IP indemnity: accept the narrowed indemnity language Jonas proposed. Add explicit exclusion for claims stemming from customer-supplied data or customer modifications.

3) Warranty and SLA: we keep SLA credits as the exclusive remedy, capped at one month’s fees. No refund-only language.

4) Commercial discount: approve 35% first-year discount only if the customer signs a 24-month commitment and prepays 50% of year 1 at signing. If they refuse prepay, discount reduced to 20% and require non-cancelable minimums.

5) Escalation path: If Skyline insists on a lower cap (<= $1M) or uncapped IP exposure, escalate to CEO/CFO for final decision. Finance: please model downside if we take $2M vs $1M and circulate a one-page risk delta by EOD tomorrow.

Marissa — move forward with the counter as discussed, build a DocuSign packet with the tracked redlines and the conditional commercial terms. Include the financing/prepay terms and a summary sheet for the CFO. If Skyline signs the 24-month and prepays, we’ll go to Ops for capacity planning.

Aditya Rao
Chief Revenue Officer
